source_text: A six-month four-day-week trial across 40 employers in an example region published its results on 2026-10-20. Participating teams cut recurring meetings by about a third before shortening the week, and most employers kept the schedule after the trial (S1).

outline: Claim: shorter weeks follow from fewer meetings, not the other way round.
Evidence: teams in the trial cut recurring meetings by about a third before shortening the week (S1).
Lesson: audit your recurring meetings before you debate the calendar.
